turns.speaker: AGENT
turns.text: Okay, I would be happy to explain this to you. Collateral is basically something that you would be using as security against the repayment of your loan. For example, if you're a homeowner, or if you own land, or any other type of property, then that could be used as collateral as a basis for your loan. So for example, this is just an example, not for your specific case. Say you wanted to borrow $50 ,000, and you use your home as collateral. So we would put a lien against your home in the event that you did not repay the balance. But of course, if you make your payments on time, and you pay off the balance before, then that lien would be revoked. In the event that you did not pay, of course, we would be able to file an injunction so that anytime you refinance your home or sold that property, then we would be able to recoup our payment at that time. That is just an example. For smaller loan amounts, you would necessarily need collateral, but you would have to show that you have good credit, and that you have been using credit responsibly, and also that you have a regular source of income. Say from a regular job, like a salary job, or if you're a W2N4E, we would need at least 12 -month bank statement that shows that you're financially solvent and that you actually have the ability to make payments on the loan amount that you are seeking.
